details: US Treasury yields climbed above 5%, contributing to a global risk-off sentiment. This surge led to significant Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) outflows, totaling over $1 billion last week, marking the largest weekly redemption since January. The increased yields and subsequent flight from risk assets have pressured cryptocurrency prices, pushing Bitcoin to a three-week low.
title: US Treasury Yields Surge, Triggering $1 Billion Bitcoin ETF Outflows

details: Surging oil prices, partly driven by the ongoing Iran conflict, are intensifying concerns that global inflation will remain elevated for longer than anticipated. This inflationary pressure could compel central banks to maintain higher interest rates, consequently diminishing investor appetite for speculative assets such as cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin's price continues to be highly sensitive to these geopolitical uncertainties and the broader risk-off market sentiment.
title: Inflation Fears and Geopolitical Tensions Pressure Crypto Markets

details: Investors are closely monitoring the upcoming release of the April Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting minutes on May 20, 2026. These minutes are expected to offer crucial insights into the Federal Reserve's monetary policy stance, potentially leading to increased volatility in Bitcoin prices and affecting DeFi liquidity. Additionally, Nvidia's earnings report, scheduled between May 18-23, is highly anticipated, with the potential to significantly impact AI-linked tokens due to the strong correlation between AI equities and digital assets.
title: Key Economic Events This Week: FOMC Minutes and Nvidia Earnings
